extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing, comprising 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang; Houxing Ren; Zimu Lu; Mingjie Zhan; Hongsheng Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from multiple source datasets, converting text instructions to speech, and curating the resulting items into listening, speaking, and viewing subsets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or unsuitable instances such as corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers were removed; approximately 10% of candidates were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data were collected from 47 datasets, including 23 audio understanding datasets for listening, 22 datasets plus RoleBench for speaking, and MMMU for viewing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Texts were preprocessed for speech synthesis by replacing image-reference tokens with descriptive phrases, rewriting text for TTS readability, rephrasing multiple-choice options, evaluating generated speech with UTMOS Strong and regenerating low-quality clips, transcribing synthesized audio with Whisper-Large-v3, deduplicating with lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, validating media integrity and answer correctness, categorizing into 13 tasks, and balanced sampling.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual curators reviewed candidate items in a web-based curation tool and assigned Good or Bad verdicts with optional notes after checking media integrity, task well-posedness, and answer validity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicates were manually reviewed and removed, and approximately 10% of candidates were discarded during validation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, UTMOS Strong, Whisper-Large-v3, Whisper, Wespeaker, emotion2vec, gpt-oss-20b
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses misuse risks from role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, including identity spoofing, harassment, fraud, impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics, and proposes safeguards such as consent gating, watermarking, traceability, and safety cards.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may carry biases from source data and design choices; questions and contexts come from academic or synthetic sources, and the fixed set of 100 roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited in diversity, is mostly English except for five Chinese roles, evaluates a limited range of models, relies on automated and GPT-based scoring that may introduce noise and bias, may carry source-data biases, lacks some task coverage such as video-audio and continuous streaming scenarios, and is evaluated offline rather than in real-time interactive settings.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for researchers to evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies, and it is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: When collecting test data, we first extract diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. ... VoiceAssistant-Eval is organized into three main subsets that reflect these principles: Listening. ... Speaking. ... Viewing.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: When collecting test data, we first extract diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. ... We synthesize speech for question texts using three advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: We exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers. Approximately 10% of candidates are discarded at this stage.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We collect source data from 23 audio understanding datasets, following the practice of AirBench (Yang et al., 2024) ... For role-playing, we use the role profiles and question texts from RoleBench (Wang et al., 2023c). Other source data are from 22 datasets ... To ensure the Viewing subset covers as many image types as possible, we select MMMU (Yue et al., 2024) as the source dataset.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We preprocess the texts to ensure high synthesis quality: 1. Image references: We replace special tokens (e.g., “<image1>”) with descriptive phrases, such as “as shown in the first image.” 2. Text rewriting: We use Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (Qwen et al., 2025) to rewrite the text so it is more suitable for TTS ... 3. Multiple-Choice Questions: We rephrase the options for better readability. ... During speech synthesis, we use UTMOS Strong (Saeki et al., 2022) to evaluate the generated speech and regenerate it until the score surpasses 3.8. ... Finally, we use Whisper-Large-v3 (Radford et al., 2022) to transcribe the synthesized audio back into text and select the audio sample with the lowest word error rate. ... We improve data quality through a four-stage curation process: (1) Deduplication ... (2) Validation ... (3) Categorization ... (4) Sampling

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To operationalize the validation step described in the main text, we build a lightweight web-based curation tool that standardizes quality checks across modalities. ... Curators review each item on a single screen ... and then assign a Good or Bad verdict, along with optional notes. ... Manual review proceeds in three quick passes: (1) Media integrity ... (2) Task well-posedness ... (3) Answer validity

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Suspected duplicates are manually reviewed and removed, resulting in 15,359 samples. ... Approximately 10% of candidates are discarded at this stage.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We use Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (Qwen et al., 2025) to rewrite the text so it is more suitable for TTS ... During speech synthesis, we use UTMOS Strong (Saeki et al., 2022) to evaluate the generated speech ... Finally, we use Whisper-Large-v3 (Radford et al., 2022) to transcribe the synthesized audio back into text ... The synthesized audio is then transcribed with Whisper (Radford et al., 2022) ... For content quality, we use gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI et al., 2025) ... For emotion, we use emotion2vec (Ma et al., 2023) ... For the role-play task, we use Wespeaker (Wang et al., 2023b; 2024c) to calculate the speaker similarity

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We will maintain a data govemance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concems arise.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: In addition, because the benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, we emphasize strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards. To mitigate misuse risks (e.g., identity spoofing, harassment, fraud) ... These measures aim to enable research on personalization while minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Fourth, like many benchmarks, VoiceAssistant-Eval may carry biases from its source data and design choices. The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources (e.g., existing datasets and rewritten instructions), which might not reflect the full richness or faimess concems of real deployments. For example, the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts. These roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: First, the dataset, though sizable (10.5K curated QA items), may still be limited in diversity. Although we include five Chinese roles in the role-play task, all other prompts and evaluations are in English. ... Third, our evaluation methodology has limitations. We rely on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which, while efficient, may introduce noise and bias. ... Fifth, although we span 13 task categories, there remain gaps in task coverage and scenario realism. ... Finally, VoiceAssistant-Eval evaluates models in an offline, static manner

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We intend for researchers to use this dataset to better evaluate voice assistants and, consequently, facilitate future studies in this area. The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset is not supposed to be used, though the risk exists, for training models for cheating.
